| Maria | **Rock** | $0$ | $-2$ | $2$ |
| **Paper** | $2$ | $0$ | $-2$ |  |
| **Scissors** | $-2$ | $2$ | $0$ |  |

Earlier part 1:

Maria represents the information in the table using the following matrix:

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 2 \\ 2 & 0 & -2 \\ -2 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

$\times $

                                        .

Earlier part 2:

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 2 \\ 2 & 0 & -2 \\ -2 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

In index notation, the highlighted entry of the matrix $P$ above is ${p}_{ij},$ where$\,$

                            
                                    
                                        
                                        $i=$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        $3$                
                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                         and 
$j=$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        $2$                
                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        .

Current part:

Maria and John agreed to increase the bet. After increasing, Maria's payoff matrix became

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & -6 & 6 \\ 6 & 0 & -6 \\ -6 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

This new matrix is obtained from matrix $P$ using the scalar multiplication $kP$, where

                            
                                    
                                        
                                        $\,k=$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-1}}

questions.worked_solution:
To express $kP,$ we multiply each entry of $P$ by $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}kP & =k[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 2 \\ 2 & 0 & -2 \\ -2 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -2k & 2k \\ 2k & 0 & -2k \\ -2k & 2k & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the above result equal to the value given for $kP$ in the problem statement:

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & -2k & 2k \\ 2k & 0 & -2k \\ -2k & 2k & 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & -6 & 6 \\ 6 & 0 & -6 \\ -6 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

We can solve for $k$ by equating any two corresponding (nonzero) elements. Let's choose the top-right elements, $2k$ and $6.$ Equating these elements, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2k & =6 \\ k & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** We would get the same result by equating any two corresponding (nonzero) elements.

In each instance of the game, there are three possible outcomes for $X$:

* The result $X=-6$ occurs $3$ times out of $9$ in the payoff matrix. Therefore the corresponding probability is $\frac{3}{9}=\frac{1}{3}.$

* The result $X=-2$ occurs $3$ times out of $9$ in the payoff matrix. Therefore the corresponding probability is $\frac{3}{9}=\frac{1}{3}.$

* The result $X=6$ occurs $3$ times out of $9$ in the payoff matrix. Therefore the corresponding probability is $\frac{3}{9}=\frac{1}{3}.$

Hence, the probability mass function for $X$ is

| $X$ | $-6$ | $-2$ | $6$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(X)$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ |

Hence, $q=r=\frac{1}{3}.$

The expected value of $X$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =-6\cdot f(-6)+(-2)\cdot f(-2)+6\cdot f(6) \\  & =-6(\frac{1}{3})+(-2)(\frac{1}{3})+6(\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =-2-\frac{2}{3}+2 \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}

questions.worked_solution:
In each drawn game, both players deposit $$2$ each, or $$4$ in total, into the saving box with probability $\frac{1}{3}.$ 

Hence, the saving box will contain $$20$ dollars if Maria and John draw $5$ games.

Then, if $Y$ is the number of times a game is drawn out of $10$ possible games, then 

$$
Y∼B(10,\frac{1}{3}).
$$

So, $Y$ has the probability mass function

$$
f(y)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{10}{y}){(\frac{1}{3})}^{y}{(\frac{2}{3})}^{10-y}.
$$

Therefore, the desired probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y=5) & =f(5) \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{10}{5}){(\frac{1}{3})}^{5}{(\frac{2}{3})}^{10-5} \\  & =252{(\frac{1}{3})}^{5}{(\frac{2}{3})}^{5} \\  & =0.137,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

shared_contexts.problem:
Maria and John are playing rock, paper, scissors. In each round, the players pick one of those three objects, and the rules are that rock beats scissors, scissors beats paper, and paper beats rock. 

They decide to extend the game and make it so that the winner of each round receives $$2$ from the loser. So, for example, if Maria picks scissors and John picks rock, then Maria pays $$2$ to John.

Maria represents the money she could earn or lose after one game using the following table.

|  |  | John |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  | **Rock** | **Paper** | **Scissors** |
| Maria | **Rock** | $0$ | $-2$ | $2$ |
| **Paper** | $2$ | $0$ | $-2$ |  |
| **Scissors** | $-2$ | $2$ | $0$ |  |
